{{short description|French mathematician}}
{{use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=August 2020}}
'''Marie-Claude Arnaud-Delabrière''' (born 24 February 1963){{r|cv}} is a French mathematician, specializing in [[dynamical system]]s. She is University Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Avignon]]{{r|profile}} and a senior member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]].{{r|iufrance}}

==Education and career==
Arnaud was a mathematics student at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)]] from 1983 to 1987; she earned a bachelor's degree in 1984, an [[agrégation]] in 1985, and a [[diplôme d'études approfondies]] in 1986.{{r|cv}} She earned her doctorate in 1990 from [[Paris Diderot University]] under the supervision of [[Michael Herman (mathematician)|Michael Herman]],{{r|cv|mgp}} and completed a [[habilitation]] in 1999 at [[Paris-Sud University]].{{r|cv}}

After working as an assistant at [[Louis Pasteur University]] from 1987 to 1989, and then as a [[Attaché Temporaire d'Enseignement et de Recherche|temporary researcher]] at Paris Diderot University from 1989 to 1991, she became an assistant professor at Paris Diderot University in 1991. In 2001 she moved to Avignon as a full professor.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
In 2010, Arnaud was a speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].{{r|icm}}
In 2011 she won the {{ill|Gabrielle Sand and M. Guido Triossi Prize|fr|Prix Gabrielle-Sand}} of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] for her work on [[Hamiltonian system|Hamiltonian dynamical systems]], and in particular on the regularity of invariant curves in the [[Dynamical billiards|dynamics of billiards]].{{r|profile|sand}}
She was named to the [[Institut Universitaire de France]] as a senior member in 2013.{{r|iufrance}} She became a member of the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2020.{{r|ae}}
